newsitem.title: POLAND: Large firms key to Polish NFI valuation - analyst. [CORRECTED 14:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Large firms key to Polish NFI valuation - analyst. [CORRECTED 14:25 GMT]

text.p: The valuation of some 50 big companies taking part in the Polish mass privatisation plan is crucial for setting a price on the 15 National Investment Funds (NFI) which run them, a fund analyst said on Monday.

Piotr Lagowski, chief analyst at NFI 15, told journalists the 50 biggest companies would be the most important because under good management the weaker firms should not have much influence on the overall value of the funds.
"The value of the NFI programme should be based on value estimates of several dozen most important companies," Lagowski said.
Lagowski said the 50 biggest firms produced 40 percent of all sales and 75 percent of profits of all the companies in the scheme.
Under Poland's mass privatisation scheme 15 NFIs run more than 30 companies each.
Some 26 million adult Poles bought participation certificates in the scheme and the certificates will be exchanged into a share in each of the funds later this year.
The certificates trade on the Warsaw bourse and so will the NFI shares, but analysts are divided over how to estimate their value.

Lagowski said the best method of measuring the NFIs' price would be an estimate of free cash reserves, which the NFIs are able to generate. According to that valuation method companies run by NFI No.15 (Corrects from "the 15 funds") are worth 1.3 billion zlotys, he said.
